title: Node signals may disconnect when saving a script with errors
body:
### Tested versions

This issue has been observed for a long time-as far as I can recall, since Godot 4.2 or even earlier. It persists in the latest stable version, 4.6.2

### System information

MacOS - Tahoe 26.4.1 - Godot Engine 4.6.2 - Metal 4.0 - M5

### Issue description

I have been struggling with a persistent and frustrating issue in Godot for a long time: signals connected via the Inspector occasionally disconnect spontaneously, forcing a manual reconnection. It has been nearly impossible to reproduce consistently as the trigger remained unknown, but today I believe I have found a likely cause.



### Steps to reproduce

While working on my project, I was switching between multiple scenes and attempted to save the project several times. One of the scripts contained an error, which the Output panel kept reporting, but I ignored it while focusing on a different scene. Upon returning to the original scene, I discovered that about half of the signals had been disconnected from the scene's script.
While I cannot confirm this is the definitive root cause, I strongly suggest investigating the behavior of signal persistence when saving a project that contains script compilation errors.

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

To set up the reproduction environment, follow these steps:

1. Open a project with multiple scenes tabs open simultaneously.

2. In one of the scenes, connect several signals to a script via the Inspector.

3. Intentionally introduce (or leave) a syntax error in that scene's script.

4. Switch to a different scene tab and perform some minor changes (e.g., move an object).

5. Save the project multiple times (Command + S or Ctrl + S) while focusing on the second scene. It may take several save attempts to trigger the bug.

6. Switch back to the scene with the script error and check if the signals in the Node tab are still connected.
